Definition: a dog; hence (by euphemism) a male prostitute
BiblicalUsage: Keleb means a dog: 1 Kings 14:11 says him that dieth of Jeroboam in the city shall the dogs eat. 2 Kings 9:36 says in the portion of Jezreel shall dogs eat the flesh of Jezebel. Psalms 68:23 says thy foot may be dipped in the blood of thine enemies, and the tongue of thy dogs in the same. Isaiah 66:3 says he that sacrificeth a lamb, as if he cut off a dog's neck.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the dog is the Bible's picture of contempt: the unclean eater, the shame of the unburied, the insult to a sacrifice. I hold that the same word that shames the wicked also shows how far God will go to cleanse the unclean.
